input.quote: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of every Deliverable (defined in 1.4 to include "other work product ... created specifically for Customer") in Vendor and leaves Customer only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. That fails the preferred position (Customer owns deliverables and work product, with Vendor assignment) and also fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables. The remaining preferred limbs are already in the deal: 14.3 retains Vendor Technology for Vendor, 13.2 grants a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, and 14.4 bars joint ownership. The redline therefore makes the single directional change needed: Customer owns each Deliverable and Vendor assigns it.

ops.oldText: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.
ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.

ops.text: Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for, so 14.2 now vests every Deliverable in Customer with an assignment from Vendor; Vendor still retains Vendor Technology under 14.3 and 13.2 already grants us the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor Technology.
proposal.summary: Flip 14.2 to Customer ownership of Deliverables with Vendor assignment
